diagnostic_evidence.quote: Without loss of generality, we may assume that $|S| = |T|$, as

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of Corollary a3 reduces the arbitrary |S|,|T| case to |S|=|T| by asserting a monotonicity property of the smallest singular value under adding rows or columns. That assertion is false in general linear algebra: adding rows to a full-row-rank m x n matrix with m<n can make the smallest singular value of the resulting square matrix much smaller than the original smallest nonzero singular value, and the desired condition-number reduction does not follow.

failure_location.quote: the smallest singular value $\sigma_{m \wedge n}(A)$ of a matrix $A \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$ with $m<n$ (resp. $m>n$) is non-increasing when at most $n-m$ rows (resp. $m-n$ columns) are added.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either prove a valid singular-value argument for the rectangular cases or restrict the corollary to |S|=|T|, losing the advertised arbitrary-S contiguous-column scope.
issues.overall_effect: The first bound in Corollary a3 for arbitrary S and the second bound for unequal cyclically contiguous S and T are not established. Corollary a4, whose proof is derived from Corollary a3, is therefore unsupported for the same rectangular cases.
issues.title: Corollary a3 proof uses a false singular-value monotonicity to reduce to the square case
issues.why_classification: The source gives no valid replacement for the false reduction, and weakening the statement to square submatrices excludes a regime explicitly advertised in the abstract and corollaries.

issues.failure_explanation: The right-hand inequality is false without further normalization. For example, take n=2, m=3, A=(1/2)B where B has orthonormal columns e_1,e_2. Then sigma_2(A)=1/2, while the square submatrices have smallest singular values at most 1/4, and the displayed square-root sum is smaller than sigma_2(A). Cauchy-Binet relates determinants, not smallest singular values, so the claimed bound does not hold.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete or replace the displayed inequality with a valid statement (for example one involving determinants or a correct singular-value interlacing argument). No main theorem depends on this displayed claim.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed assertion labelled a9 is false, and the remark's proposed framework for bounding nearly square cases is invalid as written.
issues.title: Displayed inequality a9 is false for general matrices
issues.why_classification: The defect is confined to a standalone remark and can be bypassed without changing any main theorem, rate, or guarantee.
